Innkeeper, I've a thing to say.
Harald raps the wall by the door.
Three times. As if for an answer.
현명했다고 했지.\n그 말을 사흘 씹었소.\n…돌에도 맛이 있더군. 썼소:
You said it was wise.
I chewed on that three days.
…Stone has a taste. Bitter.
문은 내가 지킨다 했지.\n그래서 말해 둘 게 있소.\n늦은 값이 얼마인:
I said I'd guard this door.
So there's a thing to tell you:
what the late payment costs.
The night the mountain gate closed,
I was the one guarding it.
A guard with a fresh beard.
누가 문을 두드렸소. 세 번.\n여자 목소리였지.\n…빗장은 내 손에 있:
Someone knocked. Three times.
A woman's voice.
…The bar was in my hand.
우리 법엔 문 앞 손님을\n돌려보내는 말이 없다.\n…드워프 법은 다른가:
Our law has no words
for turning a guest from the door.
…Is dwarf law different?
…'Tis not different, orc.
The law was the same.
The hand froze, that's all.
Knocking three times, a habit.
He is still
waiting for an answer.
장로는 명을 내렸고\n나는 빗장을 걸었소.\n돌은 누가 깎든 무게가 같소:
The elders gave the order,
I dropped the bar.
Stone weighs the same, whoever cuts it.
…Still, thank you.
You're the first
ever to say that to me.
그 목소리, 아직 들려?: Do you still hear that voice?
…Not every night.
Only on snowy ones.
So in winter I stand by the door.
That was why he insisted
on the seat by the door.
If someone knocks thrice tonight,
I'll open it.
…After I answer.
A bronze key on the table.
Its hammer crest is worn smooth.
Key to the mountain gate. A guard
gets one when he steps down.
…A letter came from the mine.
They want me to train young guards.
On these knees, mind you.
I spoke of the elders.
At the letter's end was
that elder's grandson's name. Funny.
That voice I spoke of.
Last winter I didn't hear it.
…Not by this house's door.
무릎 시리면 이끼 찜질해라.\n고집만 센 늙은 경비야.\n…가르치러 가거:
Knees ache? Use a moss poultice.
Stubborn old guard.
…Go on and teach them.
The hand that set the key down
is slow to leave the table.
Go teach them how to open.
How to open, eh.
Guards learn only to close.
…So you'd have me change that.
Fine. The first lesson:
'Knock thrice, and we answer.'
A gate key on this house's door.
There's no lock it even fits.
…No lock it fits,
that's the good of it. No one
can ever lock it again.
A shut door is long remembered,
an open one soon forgotten.
…I'll open it all the same.
마당은 내가 쓸었지?\n빗자루 빚은 갚았소.\n이제 새 내기요!:
I swept the yard, didn't I?
Broom debt's paid.
Now, a new bet!
그날 밤 하늘만 봤소.\n…안 날더군. 두 배는…\n농담이오. 내가 먼저:
I watched the sky all that night.
…You didn't fly. Double's…
Jesting. I fell asleep first.
Walked with an orc hunter.
Who bags more in three days.
Three silver coins.
Ha! On dwarf legs?
I bag five before breakfast.
Polish your silver.
Short legs, long arrows.
…Crossbow bolts, mind.
Three silver is the price
of that crossbow's string.
Lose, and it's stringless shooting.
So then, be our judge.
They say witches never lie.
하! 역시 드워프 같은 마녀요.\n이기면 반을 주지.\n…지면 마당을 또:
Ha! A witch after a dwarf's heart.
I win, you get half.
…I lose, I sweep the yard again.
같이? 오크랑?\n…그럼 누가 이긴 거요?:
Together? With an orc?
…Then who's won?
If we both win,
do we both buy the ale?
…Now that's a fine bet.
Tonight's bet:
who snores first.
…I'll not lose this time.
Brynhild rolls a holed coin
along the table. She isn't smiling.
Brought your judging fee.
…I lost. The orc got one more.
Half of three coins.
같이 사냥했소.\n멧돼지 한 마리, 둘이 나눴지.\n내기는 비긴 걸로 칩:
We hunted together.
One boar, split in two.
Call the bet a draw.
이 동전은 오라비랑 건 거요.\n'누가 먼저 장가가나.'\n…갱도가 무너:
This coin's a bet with my brother.
'Who weds first.'
…The day before the shaft fell.
Still don't know who won.
So this one's
a bet still standing.
That's why she always bets.
The loser
has to come back.
Bet you'll come back in spring.
Ha! The witch, betting?
Done. One silver.
…가만, 지는 쪽이 오는 거요?\n이기는 쪽이 오는 거요?\n…둘 다 와:
…Wait, does the loser come?
Or the winner?
…Best we both come.
I'll keep that coin for you.
…Keep it?
This is my brother's debt.
그럼 됐소. 동전이 여기 있으면\n나도 여기로 오겠지.\n드워프는 빚을:
Settled, then. Coin's here,
so I'll come back here.
Dwarves leave no debts behind.
No bets today.
…No, just one.
Will it snow by morning or not.
할머니의 할머니 말이오.\n쐐기 없이 짠 들보.\n…밤새 그 생각만 했소:
Your grandmother's grandmother.
Beams joined without a wedge.
…I thought of it all night.
You said wood hardens with age,
people the opposite.
…I've aged soft.
갱목을 짜던 시절 얘기요.\n결이 꼬인 참나무를\n버팀목으로 쓴 적이 있:
Back when I built mine props.
I once used twisted-grain oak
as a shoring post.
It didn't collapse.
But an apprentice
walked with a limp after.
I've not built since.
Only fell trees.
When you fell, the tree's to blame.
하하! 베기 전에 미안하다 해.\n그럼 도끼가 가벼워져.\n…짜기 전에도:
Haha! Say sorry before you chop.
Then the axe goes lighter.
…Try it before building too.
Trees don't answer, orc.
The grain does.
Blames the trees,
yet listens to them every day.
…Build? Me?
And if a sheep gets hurt?
…Very well. I'll read the grain first.
A fold gate
opens and shuts a thousand times.
He agreed,
and his shoulders sank.
Tomorrow, one straight-grained oak.
…Don't know yet what for.
An oak wedge in Thorgrim's hand.
The knife marks are even.
Built the fold gate.
Sheep ram it, it holds.
검은 놈이 제일 세게 받더군.\n…그놈이 대장이오?:
The black one rams hardest.
…Is he the leader?
벤 것 중에 결 바른 놈이 있어서\n버리기 아까웠소.\n…그래서 이걸 깎:
One I felled had true grain.
Shame to waste it.
…So I whittled this.
그 들보에 박을 쐐기요.\n삼백 년 버틴 들보에\n백 년을 더 얹는 거지:
A wedge for that beam.
Three hundred years it's held.
This adds a hundred more.
Wood. Iron rusts.
…And this is my work.
Still, 'tis another's beam.
The innkeeper must give leave.
First time since the apprentice
those hands mean to build.
Drive it in. Carve your name.
이름? 들보에?\n…쐐기 끝에만 작게 새기지.\n삼백 년 뒤에 누가 웃게:
A name? On the beam?
…Small, on the wedge's tip only.
So someone laughs, centuries on.
Good. Those hands left no mark.
Good work
hides inside the grain.
…Ought to write
the apprentice a letter too.
이끼 사러 오던 처자: The Girl Who Came for Moss
Durga scrapes moss off the sill
and wraps it in cloth. Quick hands.
할 일 많다던 그 얼굴,\n오늘도 그대로구나.\n쯧, 이리 와. 찜질해:
That 'lots to do' face,
same as ever today.
Tsk, come. I'll make a poultice.
Told your granny to rest,
but you don't, do you?
…Knew you wouldn't listen.
Long ago, a girl used to come
to our mine to buy moss.
Hands cold as snow.
Granny, what's that moss called?
It's not in my book.
What's not in books is medicine.
…Eat it all and I'll tell you.
After the gate shut, she never came.
The moss keeps growing though.
Granny looks at me
and sees another face.
…이름은 안 물었다.\n물었으면 찾으러 갔겠지.\n그럼 나도 사라졌을 거:
…Never asked her name.
If I had, I'd have gone looking.
Then I'd have vanished too.
Dwarves remember faces.
…Yours looks a bit like hers.
쯧, 이제야 묻는구나.\n위에서 아래로. 뿌리는 두고.\n…그 처자도 그:
Tsk, asking only now.
Top to bottom. Leave the roots.
…That girl scraped it so too.
Poultice's cold. Again.
…Fine, I'll warm it.
Child, I've a thing to say.
Sit. No, this time
I'm not telling you to sit.
…I'm the one sitting.
Durga holds her teacup
in both hands. It trembles a little.
After we talked of names,
I dreamt of that girl.
…Let her tea go cold, like you.
이끼 긁은 거 봤다.\n위에서 아래로. 잘했어.\n…이제 내가 없어도 되:
Saw you scrape the moss.
Top to bottom. Good.
…You won't need me now.
손녀가 광산으로 오래.\n눈이 흐려서 이끼랑 녹을\n못 가린다고. 맞는:
Granddaughter wants me at the mine.
Says my eyes can't tell
moss from rust. She's right.
If you leave, old woman,
who warms this house's tea?
You warm your knees.
…The child here will warm the tea.
Warming the tea was always
an excuse to sit a while longer.
The witch touches the cup
and steam rises from it.
Course there's a room. I know.
…I'll stay the winter, then go.
You write to my granddaughter.
Nobody can read my hand.
Drink it before it cools.
…Truly, this time.
You said a stone breathes.
I couldn't sleep after.
…Thinking of stone.
I said I'd wait.
The stone waited.
I waited a bit less.
Our ruins, I mean.
They didn't crumble.
…Uncle sold them. Stone by stone.
Debts, it was.
Our ancestors' doorposts
became a lord's castle wall.
If it's trusting stone, me too.
Only I copy it
onto paper.
That's why chroniclers
are always short of ink.
He trusts stone, he says,
yet speaking of his uncle
he won't look at it.
I can't show you the stone below.
…알고 있소. 묻지도 않았소.\n돌을 지키는 집이\n돌을 보여 주면 안:
…I know. I didn't ask.
A house that keeps a stone
ought not show it.
Uncle fed the village
with that silver. A lean year.
Ask the stone about forgiving.
I've not managed it yet.
I'll not put it to paper.
…Least of all his name.
Flour on Ormu's palm.
He doesn't brush it off.
우리 문설주 하나를 찾았소.\n골짜기 방앗간에서\n맷돌이 되어 돌고 있더:
Found one of our doorposts.
In a valley mill,
turning as a millstone.
I spoke of a house keeping stone.
The miller
keeps that stone well too.
숙부 얘기를 했더니\n방앗간 주인이 그러더군.\n'흉년에 그 돌이 마을을:
Told the miller of my uncle.
He said: 'In the lean year,
that stone saved the village.'
A mill's millstone, now,
that price I'd know.
Dwarf stone… comes dear.
Didn't ask the price, badger.
…I'd have bought it if I had.
He won't brush off the flour.
It came from his ancestors' stone.
…Aye. As a doorpost
it fed no one.
Now it feeds a village.
Stone doesn't lie.
…That stone turns well.
A corner chip, then.
Set by the foundation stone,
it'd keep warm company.
The miller I'll pay by dressing
his millstone with my chisel.
Dwarf fashion.
오늘 빵은 그 가루로 구웠소.\n조상 맛은 안 나더군.\n…그냥 빵 맛이:
Baked today's bread with that flour.
Didn't taste of ancestors.
…Just of bread. Good bread.
…이번엔 묻소.\n양 우리 걸쇠. 헐겁소.\n…고쳐도 되오?:
…Asking this time.
Fold latch. It's loose.
…May I fix it?
Ketil sets down an anvil.
The floor groans once.
…Father's.
The forge is gone.
Only the anvil's left.
케틸 아저씨는 말 대신 망치예요!\n제가 통역해 드릴까요?:
Uncle Ketil talks with a hammer!
Shall I translate for you?
…Father said:
'Words rust. Iron doesn't.'
…Iron rusts. He lied.
An anvil weighs as much as a man.
What he carries
is a whole forge.
Set the anvil down and rest.
His back took
a long while to straighten.
…Custom dried up.
No regrets. Not Father.
Ketil holds out an iron ring.
It's still warm.
…Set the anvil down. Slept.
Dreamt of Father.
…He smiled. Father did.
…The swords he wouldn't sharpen.
First I've told anyone.
…Lighter now.
The longest conversation
in this house just ended.
…Got something to say.
A long one.
He draws breath twice,
as before lifting a hammer.
…Here, in this house,
I sleep.
Like Father's forge.
You needn't say it. I know.
…The hook. Say if it tilts.
…No. I'll check.
감자로 담갔어요! 진짜로!\n노래가 거짓말이면\n제가 참말로 만들면 되죠:
Brewed it from potatoes! Truly!
If the song's a lie,
I'll just make it true.
비약보다 센 술 가져왔어요.\n마시면 어떻게 되냐고요?\n…노래가 나와요:
Brought ale stronger than elixirs.
What happens if you drink it?
…You start singing.
Foam spills from a small cask.
It smells a little sour.
산 아래 겨울 축제에\n양조 겨루기가 있어요.\n어르신들은 저를 애 취급:
The winter fair down the mountain
has a brewing contest.
The elders treat me like a child.
With Mother's recipe
I could win…
But then it's not my ale.
Hic! I smell ale!
I'll be your judge.
One cup… no, three.
품평은 맨정신일 때\n해 주세요, 언니!:
Judge it when you're sober,
please, Erin!
Only when she speaks of her mother
does she look down at the cup.
진짜요? 마녀님이?\n…어때요? 얼굴 보니 시죠?:
Really? You, Witch?
…Well? Sour, by your face?
It's fine! Sour can be fixed.
Ale nobody will drink,
that's what can't be.
…That's better, isn't it?
Everyone says so.
…알았어요.\n근데 거품은 제 식으로 낼래요.\n그건 아무도 모를 거예요:
…All right.
But the foam I'll do my way.
No one will ever know.
오늘 밤 통은 창가에 둘게요.\n추워야 맛이 들어요.\n…저처럼요. 농담:
The cask sits by the window tonight.
Cold makes it ripen.
…Like me. Jesting!
시다고 하신 거 고쳤어요.\n…이등 했어요! 이등!\n어르신들 입이 떡:
Fixed the sourness you spotted.
…Came second! Second!
The elders' jaws dropped.
Went with Mother's ale.
Won first.
…But I wasn't glad at all.
시그뉘 술에 은화 한 닢 걸었지.\n결과는 비밀이오.\n이 애한테 물으시:
Put a silver on Signy's ale.
The result's a secret.
Ask the lass herself.
Mother sang that cauldron song
in low notes.
I sing it rising.
근데 오는 길에 숲에서\n누가 낮은 음으로 부르더라고요.\n…꼭 엄마처럼:
But in the woods on the way,
someone sang it low.
…Just like Mother.
A song the forest sings
must not be followed.
…This one, I can't say.
The song sinks low.
The hearth fire flickers a little.
Sing it in your own notes.
올라가는 음으로요?\n좋아요! 숲이 따라 부르면\n그땐 제가 이긴 거예요:
Rising notes?
Good! If the forest sings along,
then I've won!
Named my next cask.
'The Witch's Cauldron'.
…Potatoes in it. Of course.
열쇠 잘 걸려 있군.\n…녹은 안 슬었소?:
Key still hangs well.
…No rust on it?
Taught the whelps.
Knock thrice, we answer.
…They all laughed.
눈 오는 밤이군.\n문 옆 자리, 비어 있소?:
A snowy night.
Seat by the door, is it free?
Spring! I came first, didn't I?
…So I won the bet.
Coin still safe?
…Then so am I.
Where's the broom?
Yard first, then sleep.
쐐기 끝 이름 봤소?\n…아직 안 웃었소?:
Seen the name on the wedge tip?
…Not laughed yet?
Checked the fold gate first.
The grain holds well.
Beam's straight today too.
…Thanks to those hands.
That cheating of yours.
Warm the tea again today.
Winter again.
…Said there's a room. Granny's here.
Scraped the sill moss?
Top to bottom.
Brought bread from the mill.
No ancestor taste. Good, though.
I'll not ask about below.
…Just touch the foundation stone.
Practised the low notes!
…Better than the forest now.
A new cask!
First cup's yours again, Witch.
New potato ale brewed!
…Fixed the song's words too.
